issues.title: SQL injection in user lookup query
issues.description: The login query uses f-string formatting to directly interpolate user input into a SQL query. An attacker can bypass authentication by entering a username like `' OR '1'='1` which would match all users.
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries: cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE username=? AND password=?', (username, password))

issues.title: Hardcoded secret key in source code
issues.description: The SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as a string literal in the source file. This secret will be committed to version control and visible to anyone with repository access. Secrets should be loaded from environment variables or a secrets manager.

issues.title: Using MD5 for token generation
issues.description: MD5 is a cryptographically broken hash function. Using it for token generation makes tokens predictable. An attacker who knows a username can compute the same token.
issues.suggestion: Use a proper token library like PyJWT with a strong signing algorithm, or use secrets.token_urlsafe()

risk_explanation: This PR contains a critical SQL injection vulnerability and a hardcoded secret, both of which pose immediate security risks.
